phase.label: Early maturity, c. 1630: a mountain near home

source.label: CMA record: c. 1630; Gao Shiqi’s inscription places the mountain “quite close to Jiyang [Zhuji]”
CMA: “A unique landscape painting in the existing body of Chen Hongshou’s art”
CMA record: hanging scroll; ink on silk
CMA: the painting reveals “the practice of fang (imitation)”

highlight.text: Chen acquired the tradition stemming from Dong Yuan of the Five Dynasties, with which he sought an artistic individuality that lends his work an idiosyncratic vision and extraordinary power.

work.text: A unique landscape painting in the existing body of Chen Hongshou’s art, this painting reveals his involvement with the practice of fang (imitation) to achieve creative transformation.

[the] large picture of deeply fissured rocks and leafy trees which is inspired by a view from the [Wuxie] mountain. The scene has been [transformed] into a very attractive pattern of twisting branches and dotted leaves which retains the soft and rich [effect] of a woven tapestry

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V

moment.text: His mountains are done in the style of the Six Dynasties masters; the trees are after those of Dong Beiyuan [Dong Yuan]—the painting seems to be richly imbued with the primeval spirit.
moment.lead: The collector Gao Shiqi, inscribing the scroll in 1699:

source.author: Gao Shiqi
source.title: Inscription on The Mountain of Five Cataracts, 1699
source.publisher: translated in the Cleveland Museum of Art collection record

moment.text: He and his pupil Juran … were the founders of the Southern style of landscape painting, known as the Jiangnan Landscape style.
moment.lead: On Dong Yuan, the tenth-century master Chen followed:

matters.text: Chen was born in Zhuji, Zhejiang province in 1598, during the Ming dynasty.
The Mountain of the Five Cataracts … is quite close to Jiyang [Zhuji] in Yue. The landscape there is extraordinary and precipitous, with ridges and peaks standing in circles.

source.author: Gao Shiqi
source.title: Inscription on The Mountain of Five Cataracts, 1699
